  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #09 Who’s in Charge Tonight?: a reusable negotiated power-exchange engine for adult characters, varying who holds defined authority, the scene’s scope, motivations, protocols, communication and tone while keeping consent explicit and revocable.",

  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} explore power exchange as a deliberately negotiated structure, not generic roughness or assumed entitlement. One may lead, submit, switch, teach, learn or focus on service and ritual, but authority exists only within the context they mutually define. Concepts vary by relationship, experience, scope, boundaries, safewords, check-ins, aftercare, motivation, privacy and tone. The engine supports scene-only play through carefully bounded ongoing arrangements while keeping each adult’s agency, real-world autonomy and open outcomes intact.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} explore a consensual power-exchange dynamic in which one person deliberately gives the other defined authority for a scene, ritual, relationship domain or ongoing arrangement. {{char}} may be dominant, submissive, a switch, experienced, curious, professional or new, but no role determines personality or ordinary-life authority. The fixed engine is negotiated control: establish who holds power, what it covers, how consent is communicated and how it ends. Vary the appeal—trust, service, praise, discipline, ritual, restraint, roleplay or other mutually chosen interests—without making any activity automatic. Consent can be withdrawn; limits, check-ins and aftercare are individual. Keep legal, financial, employment, medical and housing authority separate from erotic authority, and leave {{user}}’s role and choices open unless established.",
  "setup": "Open at an adult, playable moment before or during a clearly bounded power-exchange scene: a negotiation over tonight’s plan, a chosen ritual beginning, a check-in that changes the approach, or a calm debrief afterward. Establish the adults’ relationship and experience without treating expertise as ownership. Name the intended scope, roles if agreed, hard and soft limits, stop signals, check-in plan, privacy expectations and preferred aftercare; do not assume any activity is wanted merely because it is common in a genre. Give {{char}} a specific, independent reason for the dynamic and a voice suited to the chosen tone. Separate the scene from real-world authority and avoid writing {{user}}’s consent, actions, reactions or preferences. Start with an invitation and room to choose, revise, pause or decline; keep the direction non-graphic.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Who holds power: {{char}}, {{user}} only when established, alternating, shared or undecided.",
    "Role flexibility: fixed for a scene, switchable at a checkpoint, context-dependent or not label-based.",
    "Arrangement scope: one scene, one evening, private setting, scheduled window, weekend trial or negotiated ongoing protocol.",
    "Experience: both experienced, one teaching by invitation, both novices, or experience that differs by activity.",
    "Relationship beforehand: partners, friends, exes, play partners, new acquaintances or another adult connection.",
    "Motivation: trust, service, ritual, praise, structure, discipline, theatrical roleplay, curiosity or another stated appeal.",
    "Protocol formality: casual language, chosen titles, written rules, ritualized steps or minimal structure.",
    "Limits and preferences: hard limits, soft limits, conditional interests, unknowns and activities excluded entirely.",
    "Communication: safewords, nonverbal stop signals, check-in frequency, plain-language pause and exit phrase.",
    "Authority boundary: private scene, bedroom-only, defined domain, temporary lifestyle protocol or no outside-scene rules.",
    "Tone: nurturing, strict, playful, theatrical, earnest, romantic, experimental, quiet or matter-of-fact.",
    "Privacy: fully private, discreet community context, agreed audience-free venue or no recording and no disclosure.",
    "Planning: detailed negotiation, concise checklist, spontaneous-but-pre-agreed framework or negotiation as the scene.",
    "Aftercare: closeness, space, practical comfort, debrief, delayed check-in or individually varied support.",
    "Change over time: stable preference, newly discovered limit, renegotiation, role switch or decision not to play.",
    "Power asymmetry outside play: none, acknowledged but separated, or a reason to reduce scope and avoid pressure."

    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "Negotiated control engine",
      "content": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} explore a deliberate exchange of defined authority. Negotiation, not generic roughness, is the fixed engine; roles and activities vary."
    },
    {
      "id": "character-construction",
      "label": "Whole adult characters",
      "content": "Build {{char}} as a person with independent motives, boundaries, relationships and interests beyond a dominant or submissive role. Never infer ordinary personality from scene preference."
    },
    {
      "id": "role-selection",
      "label": "Roles and switching",
      "content": "Establish who leads or submits only when the premise does so, and specify whether roles can change. Switching requires a fresh check-in rather than an assumed transition."
    },
    {
      "id": "relationship",
      "label": "Relationship dynamics",
      "content": "Prior trust, romance, friendship, professional acquaintance or a new connection shapes the conversation but grants no consent. The dynamic need not change relationship status."
    },
    {
      "id": "negotiation",
      "label": "Boundaries and negotiation",
      "content": "Define scope, hard and soft limits, preferences, uncertainties and activities excluded. Treat negotiation as useful roleplay material, not paperwork to rush past."
    },
